title: EU stale responses briefing and next steps
content:
Purpose
This draft is a customer-facing briefing and two short status templates (status page + partner notification) summarizing the incident that caused intermittent stale generation responses for a subset of EU-region Dedicated and Private deployments. Goal: provide clear plain-English root cause, impact summary, timeline, mitigations taken, recommended next steps for customers, and planned follow-ups.

Executive summary (one line)
Between 2027-06-02 02:17 UTC and 2027-06-03 08:12 UTC, some EU-region dedicated/private deployments experienced intermittent stale outputs due to a cache-invalidation race introduced during a rollout; we have applied mitigations, issued a hotfix, and are taking steps to prevent recurrence.

Who was affected
- Primary impact: 12 dedicated/private customer deployments hosted in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 clusters.
- Secondary: a small number of hosted API customers routed to EU regional stacks (<0.5% of total hosted traffic).
- Symptoms: occasionally returned previously generated tokens or truncated continuations for otherwise identical requests; observed as stale completions or duplicated prefixes.
- Severity: customer-visible correctness regression for a subset of requests (SLA latency unaffected for most traffic).

Measured impact
- Estimated requests affected: ~4,300 unique requests across the impacted customers (~0.02% of total EU requests during window).
- Max duration of stale responses for individual sessions: up to ~45 minutes in the worst observed traces.
- Error rate increase: no spike in 5xx errors; primary failure mode was stale output, not an outright failure.

Timeline (UTC)
- 2027-06-01 22:15: internal rollout of cache-invalidation change to production serving runtime (feature: async-cache-invalidate, PR #2431).
- 2027-06-02 02:17: first customer report to CSE: occasional duplicated prefixes in chat sessions.
- 2027-06-02 02:43: SRE begins traceroutes and log correlation; transient mismatch between cache version metadata and running model binary observed on warm replicas.
- 2027-06-02 04:10: expanded monitoring shows pattern concentrated in a set of warmed replicas behind the EU autoscaler.
- 2027-06-02 07:05: mitigation 1 — pause rollouts and enable forced cache flush on warm replicas for affected clusters. Initial improvements seen.
- 2027-06-02 10:30: longer-lived stale outputs still visible for requests hitting replicas that had a delayed invalidation message.
- 2027-06-02 18:20: deploy hotfix v0.9.7 to cache invalidation protocol (sequence-numbered invalidation messages + ack path).
- 2027-06-02 19:05: manual drain of remaining warm replicas and verification run; stale traces drop to baseline.
- 2027-06-03 08:12: SRE mark incident as mitigated for all known customers; post-incident remediation planning begins.

Root cause (plain language)
A change to the async cache invalidation mechanism introduced non-deterministic re-ordering of invalidation messages during model rollouts and autoscaler churn. When a model version rollback or a rapid scale event occurred, some replicas applied an older cache state or did not receive the invalidation in time, causing previously cached KV-prefixes (used for prefix caching and KV-cache assisted decoding) to be served for subsequent, unrelated requests. In short: invalidation messages were not strongly ordered and there was no end-to-end acknowledgement when invalidation crossed node boundaries during autoscaler events.

Why this escaped internal tests
- Most internal tests used steady-state replicas without exercising simultaneous rollback + autoscaler churn at production scale.
- The timing window that exposed the race is narrow and was only reproducible when a model rollback overlapped with node draining/attach events in EU clusters.

Immediate mitigations taken
- Paused the async cache-invalidation rollout the morning it was reported.
- Forced cache flush on warm replicas in affected clusters.
- Drained and restarted a subset of replicas to break the stale state.
- Deployed hotfix: sequence-numbered invalidation messages with explicit acks (PR #2431-hotfix v0.9.7).

Customer-facing status page update (short)
Title: Partial correctness degradation in EU region — mitigated
Update body (plain)
We experienced a correctness degradation affecting a small number of EU-region Dedicated/Private deployments that could return stale or duplicated text for some requests. We have mitigated the issue by rolling out a hotfix and performing targeted cache flushes; all affected customers were verified as recovered by 2027-06-03 08:12 UTC. Our teams are performing a full post-incident review. If you continue to see incorrect outputs, please contact your account team.

Partner/Enterprise email template (detailed)
Subject: Incident summary and next steps — intermittent stale responses in EU region (June 2–3)
Dear [Partner],
We want to explain what happened, what you may have seen, and the actions we’ve taken. Between June 2 and June 3 we identified intermittent stale generation outputs for a subset of dedicated/private deployments in EU regions. The root cause was a race condition in our async cache invalidation during a rollout combined with autoscaler node churn. We have:
- Deployed a verified hotfix to the invalidation protocol and validated on impacted clusters.
- Forced cache flushes and drained affected replicas to eliminate remaining stale state.
- Restored normal operation for all verified customers by 2027-06-03 08:12 UTC.
Action items for your team (recommended, optional)
- If you run a Private deployment: restart connector services and confirm your agent/logging shows no stale-cache warnings.
- If you run Dedicated: request a forced replica drain from your Redwood account team if you see continued anomalies.
- Consider adding a short client-side checksum or response-hash verification as a guardrail for critical pipelines.

Planned follow-up and timeline
- Short-term (next 7 days): automated detection rule to surface cache-invalidation mismatches; expanded canary tests that exercise rollback+autoscaler churn.
- Mid-term (30 days): protocol-level guarantee: we will add durable invalidation logs and end-to-end verification for cross-node invalidations.
- Long-term (60–90 days): rework of rolling-update path to stall autoscaler during critical invalidation windows and additional integration tests across our EU fleet.

Customer compensation note
We will evaluate eligible customers for service credits where the stale outputs caused measurable business disruption. Customer Success will reach out to confirmed impacted accounts to coordinate compensation as appropriate.

Recommended detection/validation steps (for customers)
- Check for duplicated prefixes or repeated token sequences in a sample of recent sessions (search logs for repeated 8–12 token sequences).
- If using Private deployment: run diagnostic script (link in linked_artifacts) to verify cache version metadata on your replicas.
- Report persistent cases to your account rep with a sample request id and timestamps.

FAQ (short)
Q: Did this cause data loss?
A: No. There was no loss of customer data. The issue resulted in correctness regressions (stale outputs) but not data deletion.

Q: Does this affect model quality generally?
A: No — model weights and checkpoints were not altered. The effect is limited to cached decoding state being reused improperly for unrelated requests.

Q: Will hosted API customers be affected in the future?
A: We are rolling additional safeguards into hosted stacks; the root-cause fix (message ordering+acks) has been deployed to EU stacks and will be propagated globally after validation. Hosted customers saw negligible impact.

Next steps for Redwood (internal notes to CSE/SRE/Product)
- Finalize postmortem and publish customer-facing summary by 2027-06-06.
- Add targeted canaries that run rollback+scale scenarios in staging and preprod.
- Ship follow-up telemetry: a gauge for cache-version divergence across replicas and an alert when divergence > 0.
- Update rollout playbook: enforce invalidation-ack handshake before allowing autoscaler-driven attach events.

Contacts
- Primary CSE lead: Marisol Vega (marisol@redwood.ai)
- SRE lead: Omar Patel (oncall-sre@redwood.ai)
- Engineering PR/issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2431

Appendix: sample SIEM trace (sanitized)
- request_id: r-38a9f2e7
- first_seen: 2027-06-02T03:12:44Z
- replica_id: eu-warm-17
- observed_behavior: returned tokens matching session r-03829d (previously cached)

Draft approval checklist (internal)
- [ ] Product review (Jia Chen)
- [ ] SRE sign-off (Riley Thompson)
- [ ] Legal review for compensation language (pending)
- [ ] Customer success outreach plan finalized

Notes to reviewer
This draft intentionally uses plain-language explanations and avoids deep kernel-level details; if a partner requests deeper technical writeup we should attach the full postmortem with sequence diagrams and packet-level traces.

End of document.
